summary: Baileys fork resolves libsignal dependency from an unpinned personal GitHub account
details: package.json declares the `libsignal` dependency as a bare GitHub source pointing at a personal account unrelated to the Baileys publisher: `"libsignal": "github:tenka-san/libsignal-node"`, with no commit SHA, tag, or integrity check. On `npm install`, the resolver fetches whatever the current HEAD of that repository is and runs any lifecycle scripts inside it, so the content executed on the installer is controlled by the owner of that third-party GitHub account and can change arbitrarily between installs without any change to this package. The static indicator on lib/Utils/generics.js (ping/GET keyword co-occurrence) is a pattern match on a cross-platform connectivity helper and is not by itself evidence of installer-side exfiltration; the primary concern is the off-registry, unpinned, non-publisher-matched dependency source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
